name: Encounter pressure and release
summary: Combat intensity becomes legible when threat arrival, spatial pressure, resource demand, and recovery produce contrasting phases instead of uninterrupted maximum load.
player_action: The player survives a pressure phase, creates an advantage, recognizes release, and uses it to reposition, recover, or choose the next risk.
system_response: The encounter changes composition, spacing, reinforcement timing, or reward state while preserving a readable path from pressure to release.
failure_modes: Maximum pressure becomes normal and loses meaning.
Release arrives before the player's decision caused it.
The encounter continues after appearing complete.
A single safe loop solves every composition.
accessibility: Expose encounter transitions through multiple channels.
Allow intensity tuning while preserving phase structure.

smallest_playable_test.setup: One looped arena with two entrances, cover, a flank route, three enemy roles, two waves, and a recoverable resource decision.
smallest_playable_test.retain_if: Players can identify why pressure rose and how their decisions created a useful release window.
smallest_playable_test.revise_if: The phases work once but become mechanically identical on repeat.
smallest_playable_test.reject_if: Success depends on waiting in one position or enduring undifferentiated overload.

evidence.claim: Hades varied chamber timing, enemy composition, room size, attack presentation, and reward feedback together rather than treating encounter pacing as spawn count alone.
evidence.notes: Patch evidence supports coordinated encounter tuning; the pressure-release model remains a testable synthesis.
